alignments.note: Causal conjunction; the ASV's clause-initial *For* answers to it, while the later *for* (t004) belongs to πρός.
Substantival article supplying the subject pronoun *they* under rule 22; no participle follows it, so rule 32 is not in question.
Correlative μέν; rule 70 aligns it where the ASV writes a word for it, and here it writes *indeed*. The answering δέ keeps its own *but*.
Preposition of duration rendered by *for* (rule 36).
Attributive adjective; rule 58 gives the supplied determiner to the noun, leaving the adjective a bare *few*.
Anarthrous noun taking the supplied determiner under rule 58, discontinuously across the adjective under rule 15.
Finite verb with its supplied English object *us*, a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it (rule 74's object arm); rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it `added`.
Preposition governing the articular participle, realized by the clause-introducing *as* (rule 61's principle that the governing preposition takes the English introducer).
Nominalizing article of the substantivized participle; the ASV recasts κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν as a finite clause and writes no word answering to the article (rules 23 and 61).

Participle rendered *seemed good*. Head on *seemed* under rule 91: the corpus spends *seem* and *think* on δοκέω, and *good* is the completion the English idiom supplies. Heading on *good* as a meaning-bearing complement under rule 17 is the competing reading, but δοκέω's own gloss is the verb word.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along (rule 21), headed on the pronoun.
Adversative conjunction answering μέν; rule 70 keeps its own *but* on it.
Substantival article supplying the subject pronoun *he* under rule 22.
Preposition rendered *for*; rule 36 keeps the English preposition on the Greek preposition.

Article realized by the supplied possessive *our*. No other source word stands in this phrase to take it, so rule 20's second arm applies rather than displacement; rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it `added`.
Substantivized participle rendered by the noun *profit*.
Preposition governing the articular infinitive, taking the English clause-introducer *that* under rule 61; rule 24 makes this one analysis with εἰς τό rendered *to the end that*.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive, `unrepresented` under rules 61 and 23.
Infinitive expanded into a finite clause; the supplied subject *we* is a rule 74 helper on the infinitive and the auxiliaries ride along under rule 9, headed on the lexical *partakers* under rule 17.
Article displaced by the genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ → *his* (rule 20); *of* stays with the noun.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *his*.
Noun with its case preposition *of*, which rule 20 leaves on the noun where a possessive has displaced the article; headed on the noun under rule 17.

review_notes: All 22 source ids and all 27 target ids partitioned exactly once.

Three `unrepresented` units, all articles: the two nominalizing articles of the articular participle and infinitive (rules 23, 61) and the article displaced by αὐτοῦ (rule 20). The article at s015 is deliberately not among them, no competitor being present for the supplied *our*.

Heads reviewed separately from edges: δοκοῦν heads on *seemed* per rule 91's lemma test rather than on the complement *good*, and μεταλαβεῖν heads on *partakers* rather than on the supplied subject or auxiliaries.
